messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The quiet changes are adding up — people are acting like things will last, and the signals, though subtle, are all pointing in the same direction. Be careful, but stay sharp; the moment may be closer than it seems."
Sender 2: "The air’s changed — people are talking openly again, and even the silence from the top feels louder than noise. Just keep your eyes open and your words light; something’s shifting, and we’re not the only ones noticing."
Sender 3: "The kids’ school is back on schedule, football’s packed, and the permits are still sitting in limbo — everything’s normal, but the silence feels heavier than noise. Just keep an eye on the little things; the quiet’s not peace, it’s the calm before someone decides to move."
Sender 4: "The air feels different lately—people are talking, even strangers. I’ve been keeping my head down, but something’s shifting beneath the surface, and the usual signs aren’t adding up. Be careful what you say, and keep your eyes open."
Sender 5: "Just wanted to say — the air’s changed. People are moving differently, quieter, but with a kind of calm I haven’t seen in years. Not hopeful, exactly. Just… ready. Be careful what you say, but don’t pretend it’s not happening."
Sender 6: "The markets are talking louder than the state, and the silence from the top is starting to feel like a countdown. Be careful what you say — even the air seems to be listening."
Sender 7: "The air’s changed—people are talking openly now, not just complaining. Whatever’s happening, it’s not just noise. Be careful, stay sharp, and keep your ears open."
Sender 8: "Just got word from someone reliable — things are quiet on the surface, but the undercurrents are shifting. The schools haven’t paid teachers in weeks, yet no one’s panicking. Feels like everyone’s waiting to see who blinks first."
Sender 9: "The air’s different lately—people aren’t whispering anymore, and even the usual silence around certain topics feels… thinner. I’ve been keeping my ears open, and whatever’s coming, it’s not just talk."
Sender 10: "The kids are getting new backpacks for school — seems like they’re finally starting to stock up on supplies. Nothing official, just… more of everything, all at once. Be careful what you say, even the quiet ones are listening."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
